sources.title: Articles on Smashing Magazine — For Web Designers And Developers

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Preethi Sam)
articles.description: What can we do to make a mobile app better? What subsidiary features are worth providing for our users? I have some ideas. You might, too. So, let’s compare our notes. Without any prescriptions attached, here are seven features I believe can palpably improve a user’s experience with a mobile app.
articles.title: The Things Users Would Appreciate In Mobile Apps

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Tatsiana Tarkan)
articles.description: Tatsiana Tarkan digs deep into iconography as part of a design system and shares some doable tips that will turn icon creation and maintenance into an enjoyable process.
articles.title: Iconography In Design Systems: Easy Troubleshooting And Maintenance

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Silvestar Bistrović)
articles.description: Remember the HTML `` element? It’s deprecated, so it’s not like you’re going to use it when you need some sort of horizontal auto-scrolling feature. That’s where CSS comes in because it has all the tools we need to pull it off. Silvestar Bistrović demonstrates a technique that makes it possible with a set of images and as little HTML as possible.
articles.title: Infinite-Scrolling Logos In Flat HTML And Pure CSS

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Cosima Mielke)
articles.description: Could there be a better way to welcome the new month than with a little inspiration boost? We might have one for you: desktop wallpapers created by the community for the community. Enjoy!
articles.title: Colorful Blossoms And Rainy Days (April 2024 Wallpapers Edition)

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Victor Ayomipo)
articles.description: There’s no shortage of articles about the mental health of developers, ranging from personal accounts of harrowing work experiences to round-ups of advice on how to preserve healthy work habits. But what working situations trigger things like stress, anxiety, burnout, and depression? Victor Ayomipo shares his personal triggers and how he manages them.
articles.title: How Developers Can Strengthen Their Mental Health Amidst High-Pressure Projects

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Cosima Mielke)
articles.description: Based on responses from over 1,200 product professionals, Maze’s Future of User Research Report uncovers how product teams conduct research to inform decision-making and build successful products. Learn about the top three trends defining the user research industry in 2024 and beyond.
articles.title: The Future Of User Research: Expert Insights And Key Trends

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Henry Bley-Vroman)
articles.description: There are many ways to approach a “Dark Mode” feature that respects a user’s system color scheme preferences and allows for per-site customization. Henry Bley-Vroman walks through a new possibility that leans into cutting-edge CSS, with minimal JavaScript to support persisting the user’s color scheme preference across pages.
articles.title: Setting And Persisting Color Scheme Preferences With CSS And A “Touch” Of JavaScript

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Chiara Aliotta)
articles.description: Whether digital or physical, designing a customer touchpoint requires an understanding of the essential relationship between the brand and the user experience, which is also known as the **brand experience.** This article is a simple guide to building long-lasting customer relationships based on the seven rules of Rikyu in the Japanese tea ceremony for a creative and memorable twist.
articles.title: Crafting Experiences: Uniting Rikyu’s Wisdom With Brand Experience Principles

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Vitaly Friedman)
articles.description: It’s here, and it’s shipping! Meet our newest Smashing book, ”Success at Scale”. It’s filled with practical insights and real-world case studies of how big changes can be made on projects of any size. Addy Osmani has curated finest examples, case studies and interviews to help you get successful at scale. Jump to the details and get the book right away.
articles.title: Now Shipping: Success At Scale, A New Smashing Book by Addy Osmani

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Krisztina Szerovay)
articles.description: How was the first SmashingConf in Antwerp, you ask? One of our online attendees, Krisztina Szerovay, shares her sketchnotes and takeaways of the talks that were held on both days of the conference — with photos and recordings saved as best for last. [See you live in Antwerp this year, maybe?](https://smashingconf.com/antwerp-2024)
articles.title: Sketchnotes And Key Takeaways From SmashingConf Antwerp 2023

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Temani Afif)

articles.description:
nikitonsky: What a useless little dialogue. It usually happens when you are trying to connect to a public Wifi but fail. iOS gives you three options:
- Use Without Internet. Why would I want to do that? “I cannot send email. Mark it as Sent anyways?”
- Use Other Network. Sounds okay, but useless most of the time. People don’t usually have a list of networks they want to try. I tried one network, it didn’t work, let’s just forget about it.
- Cancel. Cancel what? This dialog appears out of nowhere, waaay after you first tried to connect to Wifi. Basically it’s a result of some internal check iOS does, not a user’s action.
#iOS #iPhone #Wifi

articles.author: sil
articles.description:
I’ve recently switched back from vscode to Sublime Text, which means that after all the time I spent training my fingers to type “code somefile.txt” instead of “subl somefile.txt” I now need to undo all that conditioning and go back to subl again. So I thought, hey, maybe I should dump a little shell script called code in my bin folder which admonished me in some amusing way, thus Pavlov-ing myself into learning to do it right.
And then I thought, hey, what’d be cool is if I had that Matrix-esque “raining code” effect in the Terminal and then it was superimposed with a box saying “STOP TYPING code AND USE subl INSTEAD”, like the “SYSTEM ERROR” message at the end of the first movie.
And then I thought: someone’s already done this, right? And they have; it is called cmatrix. But I don’t like cmatrix because it doesn’t do the colours right; the text just sorta stops rather than fading away like the movie does, and it feels unreal and too sharp for me. Now, don’t get me wrong, I understand why this is; terminals support a full proper range of colour these days, but writing a program which gets released to actual people and which can deal with the bewildering array of terminal settings out there is a miserable waste of everyone’s time. But I’m not writing this for anyone else; it only has to work in my terminal (in true works on my machine fashion). And this will give me a chance to noodle about with Python terminal libraries such as blessed to make something interesting. Hence, matrix24.py:


It’s a bodge all round, and it still doesn’t look right, and Jess pointed out that making something cool happen when I make a mistake is the opposite of conditioning, but I got to fiddle about with a new library for a bit, so that was fun. Can I do something productive now?
(title from a classic post about the Matrix which still makes me laugh even after all these years, although it is very unfair to Keanu Reeves who is a cool bloke and should be emulated in his approach to life)
articles.title: The Matrix has you, part 2

articles.description:
• Fler chefer än medarbetare upplever höga stressnivåer. Det visar en ny rapport av koncernen Falck.

  • Rapporten visar att 36% av cheferna upplever en stress på en nivå som kan utgöra hälsorisker och motsvarande var det 30% av medarbetarna som upplevde samma sak.

  • Psykologen Lena-Karin Allinger som gjort studien menar att en anledning är kravet på att konstant vara tillgänglig.
articles.title: Ny rapport: Stress allt vanligare bland chefer

articles.description:
• Moderaterna står fast vid nya könstillhörighetslagen – det beskedet kommer från partiets gruppledare i riksdagen efter att partiets riksdagsgrupp, där frågan är infekterad, haft ett två timmar långt extrainsatt möte nu på fredagseftermiddagen.

  • Det är bland annat förslaget om att sänka åldersgränsen för den som vill byta juridiskt kön i folkbokföringen som väckt intern kritik i Moderaterna.

  • Den 17 april skall riksdagen rösta om den nya könstillhörighetslagen som alla riksdagspartier utom SD och KD står bakom.
articles.title: Moderaterna står fast vid ny könstillhörighetslag

articles.description:
• Ryssland har på senare tid intensifierat sina attacker mot den ukrainska storstaden Charkiv.

  • På fredagseftermiddagen hördes explosioner i staden och natten innan skedde två massiva drönarattacker i rad där tre räddningsarbetare dödades i den senare attacken.

  • Enligt experter agerar Ryssland på det här sättet för att hindra hjälp från att komma fram, rapporterar Sveriges Radios Ukrainakorrespondent Lubna El-Shanti.
articles.title: El-Shanti: ”Ryssland inväntar räddningspersonal – och slår till igen”
Hör senaste nyheterna i Ekot kvart i sex

articles.description:
• Idag är det den sista fredagen i den muslimska högtiden Ramadan, och det har kommit uppmaningar att samlas vid Al Aqsa-moskén i Jerusalem vid fredagsbönen för att protestera mot Israel och kriget.

  • Samtidigt har Iran utlovat en hämndattack mot Israels för den attack mot det iranska konsulatet i Damaskus där en högt uppsatt general dog, vilket oroar många.

  • ”En ung tjej i sa att det kändes som att hon levde i början av tredje världskriget”, säger korrespondenten Love Lyssarides som är på plats i Jerusalem.
articles.title: Läget i Israel: Växande oro efter hot om hämndattack från Iran

articles.description:
• Israel stängde sin ambassad i Stockholm på fredagen, rapporterar Aftonbladet.

  • De israeliska ambassaderna i ett 30-tal andra länder hålls också stängda med anledning av konflikten med Iran.

  • ”Vi är oroade för att attacker kan komma att ske. Därför håller vi stängt”, säger en anställd vid Stockholmsambassaden till tidningen.
articles.title: Israel har stängt ambassaden i Stockholm
Turerna kring den nya lagen om könstillhörighet

articles.description:
• Huvudmannen för Darknet-sajten Flugsvamp 3.0, en handelsplats för droger på nätet, dömdes idag till elva år och tio månader för synnerligen grovt narkotikabrott.

  • ”Ingenting har sedan avslutad förhandling pekat i den här riktningen”, säger mannens försvarsadvokat Kinora Awrohum.

  • Enligt Kinora Awrohum har försvaret presenterat egen bevisning och visat på alternativa gärningsmän och hon räknar med att domen kommer överklagas.
articles.title: Försvarsadvokaten efter domen: ”Kom som en chock”

articles.description:
• En 41-årig man dömdes på fredagen i ett omfattande narkotikamål, som rör Flugsvamp 3.0, en handelsplats för droger på internet. Sajten hade en omsättning i miljardklassen.

  • Mannen, som enligt domen startade sajten, döms till fängelse i elva år och tio månader.

  • Två andra personer döms till fängelse, i sex och ett halvt år respektive fyra och ett halvt år, för medhjälp till synnerligen grovt narkotikabrott. De dömda nekar till brott.
articles.title: Drev knarksajt på darknet – döms till elva års fängelse

articles.description:
• En man som misstänks ha drivit sajten Flugsvamp 3.0 döms till fängelse i elva år och tio månader för synnerligen grovt narkotikabrott, meddelar Stockholms tingsrätt. Åklagaren hade yrkat på 14 års fängelse.

  • Enligt mannens advokat kommer de att överklaga domen.

  • Två medåtalade män döms till fängelse i sex år och sex månader respektive fyra år och sex månader för bland annat medhjälp till synnerligen grovt narkotikabrott.
articles.title: Drev knarksajten Flugsvamp 3.0 – döms till elva års fängelse

articles.description:
• Den nya könstillhörighetslagen, som nu är färdigbehandlad och som riksdagen skall rösta om den 17 april har har skapat stor dramatik.

  • Moderaternas riksdagsgrupp håller i eftermiddag ett extrainsatt möte, med anledning av turbulensen kring könstillhörighetslagen, och samtidigt kräver nu Sverigedemokraterna att förslaget som riksdagen planerat att rösta om.

  • Nu skickas tillbaka till socialutskottet, det säger partiets gruppledare Linda Lindberg.
articles.title: Stor dramatik runt nya könstillhörighetslagen

articles.description:
• Gränsövergången Eretz mellan Israel och Gazaremsan öppnas nu efter påtryckningar från USA, bland annat i ett telefonsamtal mellan Joe Biden och Benjamin Netanyahu.

  • Biden kallade den humanitära situationen i Gaza ”oacceptabelt”, det skarpaste uttalandet från Vita huset sedan Hamas attack mot Israel den 7 oktober, säger Ekots Mellanösternkorrespondent Cecilia Uddén.

  • ”Ett starkt ord i diplomatiska sammanhang”, säger Cecilia Uddén.
articles.title: Uddén: Israeliska företrädare har sagt att hungersnöden är nonsens

articles.description:
• Sverigedemokraterna kommer att försöka stoppa förslaget om juridisk könstillhörighetslag. Partiet vill skicka tillbaka förslaget till socialutskottet, enligt ett pressmeddelande.

  • Den nya könstillhörighetslagen innebär bland annat att det ska bli lättare att ändra juridiskt kön.

  • ”De vill helt enkelt bromsa processen, eller helst stoppa den helt”, säger Ekots politikkommentator Helena Gissén.
articles.title: Gissén: ”SD tar tillfället i akt nu när det börjat storma”

articles.description:
• Mer nödhjälp måste nå befolkningen i Gaza.

  • Sverigedemokraterna försöker stoppa förslaget om könstillhörighetslag.

articles.title: Uppdatera dig med Lunchekot

articles.description:
For the first time, potential signs of the rainbow-like ‘glory effect’ have been detected on a planet outside our Solar System. Glory are colourful concentric rings of light that occur only under peculiar conditions. 
 
Data from ESA’s sensitive Characterising ExOplanet Satellite, Cheops, along with several other ESA and NASA missions, suggest this delicate phenomenon is beaming straight at Earth from the hellish atmosphere of ultra-hot gas giant WASP-76b, 637 light-years away. 
 
Seen often on Earth, the effect has only been found once on another planet, Venus. If confirmed, this first extrasolar glory will reveal more about the nature of this puzzling exoplanet, with exciting lessons for how to better understand strange, distant worlds.
articles.title: First ‘glory’ on hellish distant world?

articles.description: On 8 April 2024, a great swath of the United States and Mexico will experience a total solar eclipse, with viewers getting the rare chance to see the Sun’s stunning outer atmosphere.
articles.title: Solar Orbiter to watch for eruptions during total eclipse

articles.description: The NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope has set its sights on the starburst galaxy Messier 82 (M82), a small but mighty environment that features rapid star formation. By looking closer with Webb’s sensitive infrared capabilities, a team of scientists is getting to the very core of the galaxy, gaining a better understanding of how it is forming stars and how this extreme activity is affecting the galaxy as a whole.
articles.title: Webb probes galaxy teeming with newborn stars
Solar Orbiter prepared for ‘worst-case scenario’

articles.description: In the run up to April’s total solar eclipse, ESA-led Solar Orbiter and NASA-led Parker Solar Probe are both at their closest approach to the Sun. Tomorrow, they are taking the opportunity to join hands in studying the driving rain of plasma that streams from the Sun, fills the Solar System, and causes dazzlement and destruction at Earth.
articles.title: ESA and NASA team up to study solar wind

Image:
			
A citizen scientist digging through data from the ESA/NASA Solar and Heliospheric Observatory has found the mission’s 5000th comet.
The tiny comet – indicated between the vertical lines in the inset – belongs to the ‘Marsden group’, named after the British astronomer Brian Marsden, who first recognised the group based on SOHO observations. Marsden group comets are thought to be pieces shed by the much bigger Comet 96P/Machholz, which SOHO observes as it passes close to the Sun every 5.3 years.
This 5000th comet was discovered by Hanjie Tan, an astronomy PhD student in Prague, Czechia. Hanjie has been comet hunting since he was just 13 years old, discovering over 200 comets since 2009.

articles.title: SOHO reaches 5000 comets

In the year 1181 a rare supernova explosion appeared in the night sky, staying visible for 185 consecutive days. Historical records show that the supernova looked like a temporary ‘star’ in the constellation Cassiopeia shining as bright as Saturn.
Ever since, scientists have tried to find the supernova’s remnant. At first it was thought that this could be the nebula around the pulsar (dead star) 3C 58. However closer investigations revealed that the pulsar is older than supernova 1181.
In the last decade, another contender was discovered; Pa 30 is a nearly circular nebula with a central star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It is pictured here combining images from several telescopes. This composite image uses data across the electromagnetic spectrum and shows a new spectacular …
articles.title: Marvel at stunning echo of 800-year-old explosion

articles.description:
Image:
			
Astronomers have created the largest yet cosmic 3D map of quasars: bright and active centres of galaxies powered by supermassive black holes. This map shows the location of about 1.3 million quasars in space and time, with the furthest shining bright when the Universe was only 1.5 billion years old.
The new map has been made with data from ESA’s Gaia space telescope. While Gaia’s main objective is to map the stars in our own galaxy, in the process of scanning the sky it also spots objects outside the Milky Way, such as quasars and other galaxies.
The graphic representation of the map (bottom right on the infographic) shows us the location of quasars from our vantage point, the centre of the sphere. The regions empty of quasars are where the disc of our galaxy blocks our view.
